In a school during the 1980s, swimming class was a mandatory part of the curriculum, held twice a week without exception. Students were required to don their swimsuits and prepare for the pool during the fourth period. However, an unusual pattern began to emerge—bomb threats coincidentally occurred every time the students were gearing up for their swim class.

The entire school would be evacuated, with police and sniffer dogs arriving to investigate the potential threat. This chaotic scene repeated itself weekly for about a month, leaving teachers and the principal in a state of panic, unsure of how to handle the situation.

Unbeknownst to everyone, the culprit was a single student who despised swimming. Unable to swim and filled with dread at the thought of the class, he devised a plan to avoid it. Each swim day, he would sneak off campus, head to a nearby gas station, and use the pay phone to call in a fake bomb threat. Remarkably, he did this using his normal voice, simply stating, "Yeah, there's a bomb at the school. You should probably check on it."

Eventually, his scheme was uncovered. He was caught and suspended for two weeks, with the added consequence of having to retake the swimming class during the summer. This audacious and elaborate plan became the most outrageous way anyone had ever skipped gym class.
